# Captain Saul

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventy-six years old in Volume 4  <sub>[v4 c8 P44](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0044), [v4 c9 P15](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0015), [v4 c16 P18](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0018)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c39 P28](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0028)</sub>
- **Origin:** St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v4 c16 P18](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0018), [v4 c30 P35](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0035)</sub>
- **Role:** Lighthouse keeper at Seven Gulls Point; former sea captain  <sub>[v4 c5 P1](../source/v04-c05.md#nw-v04-c05-p0001), [v4 c7 P27](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0027), [v4 c9 P15](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0015)</sub>
- **Titles:** Captain
- **Nicknames:** Captain Saul

## Appearance

Captain Saul is a tall, slightly stooped man with a muscular frame that suggests great former strength. He has a weather-beaten, bronzed, heavily furrowed face with a broad forehead, a rough mouth, and thin, firm jaws. He has a thick, iron-gray mane of hair that hangs down to his shoulders, and deep-set, exceptionally blue eyes.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P12](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0012), [v4 c6 P13](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0013), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015), [v4 c20 P6](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0006), [v4 c31 P18](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0018)_

## Personality

Captain Saul is a warm, polite, and deeply compassionate man with a simple, childlike faith and an intense love for beauty. He possesses an innate, unselfish desire to care for animals and individuals in need, regardless of the personal cost. A natural-born storyteller, he takes immense joy in sharing his past adventures and life experiences. He meets hardship and the approach of old age with a serene, patient, and humorous philosophy, viewing every part of life as a gift.

_Sources: [v4 c6 P12](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0012), [v4 c6 P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 c6 P23](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0023), [v4 c6 P25](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0025), [v4 c7 P49](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0049), [v4 c8 P18](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0018), [v4 c8 P20](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0020), [v4 c9 P20](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0020), [v4 c17 P17](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0017), [v4 c17 P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018)_

## History

In his youth, Captain Saul befriended John Tremayne, the local schoolmaster, and helped him prepare a small cottage at Seven Gulls for his incoming bride, Damaris Leigh. After their wedding, Saul ran away to sea, spending over fifty years sailing the globe as a sea captain and experiencing numerous shipwrecks, mutinies, and adventures. In his early adulthood, he suffered the loss of his sweetheart, Margaret, who drifted out to sea during a storm; he never married, remaining devoted to her memory for the rest of his life. After retiring to Seven Gulls Point, he served as the keeper of the Seven Gulls lighthouse, residing there with his beloved pet cat, the First Mate. He formed deep friendships with his new neighbors, Dr. Hugh Carrow and his wife Nell, frequently entertaining them at the lighthouse with tales of his seafaring days.

In his later years, Captain Saul assisted Lorna Vane by lending her money and taking in her disabled husband, Rufus, for days at a time to ease her burden. He also welcomed Adrian Treleaven, the grandson of John Tremayne, to stay at the lighthouse and compile his life's journal into a book. Shortly after the book was published and delivered to him, Captain Saul passed away peacefully in his sleep at the lighthouse, holding his completed 'life-book' in his hands. He was buried near the old Seven Gulls churchyard, leaving his cherished curiosities to Nell's son, Little Kit, and his cat to the care of Nell and Hugh.

## Background by volume

- Came from a long line of seafaring people  <sub>[v4 c6 P12](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0012)</sub>
- Ran away to sea as a young boy after his friend John Tremayne's marriage  <sub>[v4 c7 P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048)</sub>
- Lost his sweetheart, Margaret, when she was swept out to sea in a dory fifty years prior  <sub>[v4 c20 P12](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0012), [v4 c20 P15](../source/v04-c20.md#nw-v04-c20-p0015)</sub>
- Spent fifty years traveling the globe as a sea captain before retiring to Seven Gulls Point  <sub>[v4 c8 P18](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0018), [v4 c16 P18](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0018)</sub>
- Discovered the amnesiac Laurence Vane in Havana and brought him back home to St. Brendan's Island  <sub>[v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c32 P6](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0006)</sub>
